chunks: A group narrated to me from al-Tala'kbari from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi from al-Husayn ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Razin who said: Abul Hasan al-Mawsili al-Khubayri narrated to me saying: My father narrated that he frequently visited Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Sarmarrah, and that one day he came to him and found that his mount had been brought for him to ride to the palace of the ruler. He was discolored from anger. A man from the common people used to come to him; whenever the Imam mounted, he would pray for him and bring items to accompany him, but the Imam (peace be upon him) disliked this. On that day, the man increased in speech and persisted, so they rode until they reached a fork in the road. One of the paths was narrow due to the animals, so he took a path to exit and meet him there. The Imam (peace be upon him) called one of his servants and said to him: Go and shroud this man. The servant followed him. When the Imam (peace be upon him) reached the market and we were with him, the man came out of the alley to confront him. A mule was standing at that spot, and it kicked him and killed him. The boy stood and shrouded him as commanded, and the Imam (peace be upon him) proceeded and we followed him.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s)
key_terms.سَرْمَنَ الرَأْيِ: Sarmarrah, the city in Iraq where the Imams resided

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the man who was killed by a mule in the presence of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s)?
ai.summary: This incident from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Imam’s precise knowledge of the unseen (*‘ilm al-ghayb*) and the reality of divine decree (*mashi’a*), where the command to shroud precedes the actual death. It serves as a key proof for the Shia doctrine of the Imam’s infallibility and his ability to predict specific events, reinforcing his status as the *Hujjah* (proof) of God on earth during the Minor and Major Gheyba periods.
